chunks: And it is narrated from Dāwūd ibn Sirḥān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I had with me two sacks of musk; one of them was moist and the other dry. I began with the moist one and sold it. Then I took the dry one to sell, and I found that I was not given for the dry one the price that it was worth, and they would not increase me beyond the price of the moist one. So I asked him about that: would it be proper for me to mix it? He said: 'No, unless you inform them.'
He said: So I mixed it, then informed them. He said: 'There is no harm in it if you inform them.'

key_terms.الثَّمَنَ: the price or sale value of the commodity
key_terms.تُعْلِمَهُمْ: to inform them clearly about the matter
key_terms.جِرَابَانِ: two sacks or containers used for holding the musk
key_terms.رَطْبٌ: moist, describing one quality of the musk
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible
key_terms.يَابِسٌ: dry, describing the other quality of the musk

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islamic law to mix goods of different quality before selling them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding sale disclosure and fairness in trade. It permits mixing goods of differing qualities only when the buyers are clearly informed, thereby preventing deception and protecting honesty in transactions.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3839 - It is narrated from Dawood bin Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (as), who said:

I had two sacks of musk-one was moist, and the other was dry. I started with the moist one and sold it.
Then I took the dry one to sell, but I found that I was not offered the price it was worth, and they would not pay me more than the price of the moist musk.
So I asked Imam (as) about that, whether it was permissible for me to mix them.
Imam (as) said: "No, unless you inform them."

He said: "So I mixed them and then informed them."
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it if you inform them."
